section_entries.label: Proof of the moment asymptotic
section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses Perron inversion and a contour shift to turn the poles at 1 and 3/4 into the polynomial main term and exceptional secondary term under the assumed growth bound.

unit_result_entry.title: Convert the w=3/4 pole into an x^(3/4) secondary main term
unit_result_entry.why_material: Perron inversion, shifting from Re(w)>1 to Re(w)=sigma_0+epsilon, and balancing the vertical-growth and truncation errors show exactly how the order-seven pole at 1 yields xR_3(log x) while the simple pole at 3/4 yields the exceptional secondary term.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Only the principal-character Euler product survives the limiting residue
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof reduces all residue contributions to Euler products R(chi,chi',chi''), shows via orders of L- and zeta-factors that every contribution with a nontrivial character vanishes, and retains the principal-character term to obtain the explicit nonzero residue.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: A functional-equation orbit can reveal a hidden polar contribution, but it becomes a genuine secondary term only after nonvanishing survives arithmetic projection and contour shifting is controlled.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This source proves the residue computation conditionally on continuation assumptions and derives the unweighted asymptotic only under a separate growth bound.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Pole orbit to secondary asymptotic

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The reach of meromorphic continuation and the vertical growth exponent jointly determine whether a transported pole can be separated from the contour error in an unweighted moment asymptotic.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The desired stronger growth estimate is suggested by symmetry and Phragmen-Lindelof reasoning but is not obtained here.
